newsitem.title: USA: EBITDA scuttles Heartland Wireless debt.
newsitem.headline: EBITDA scuttles Heartland Wireless debt.

text.p: Debt of Heartland Wireless Communications tumbled about 20 points on Friday in response to a significant drop in fourth quarter cash flow, traders and analysts said.

Heartland Wireless late on Thursday said its Q4 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) results were a loss of $9.6 million, compared to a loss of $0.4 million for the same period one year earlier.
The results included a one-time $9.1 million charge, including $5.2 million for bad debt and a reserve for uncollectable accounts receivable, the company said.

Heartland's 14 percent debt, issued last December, traded down to a 45 bid, 50 offer market from a 65 bid, 70 offer market at the close on Thursday, traders said. The Heartland 13 percent debt fell to a 40 bid, 45 offer market from a 60 bid, 65 market.

The EBITDA Q4 loss came as a surprise to the Street despite an announcement by Heartland in late February that warned analysts expectations were too high, said one analyst who declined to be named. EBITDA expectations that ranged from flat to up $2 million were revised to down $1 million after the company's announcement, he said.

"They were one of the few wireless cable companies in the third quarter that were cash flow positive, and even after they told the market (EBITDA) had turned negative nobody thought the numbers would be this bad," the analyst said.

Heartland on Monday reported the resignation of three executives, including senior vice president and chief financial officer John Bailey, as part of a management and operational restructuring. John A. Fanning, interim president and chief executive officer of Heartland, will assume the duties of Bailey until a replacement is named, Heartland said.
The Plano, Texas based firm owns and operates wireless cable TV systems in small- to mid-size markets. Its senior debt is rated B3 by Moody's Investors Service and single-B by Standard & Poor's.
